name: UI Sources
tagline: Retired mobile-UX interaction library; the domain now 301s to ScreensDesign
description: UI Sources was a library of recorded mobile app interactions and flows, catalogued by app and by UX pattern. The domain no longer serves its own site: https://uisources.com returns a 301 to https://screensdesign.com/, and the ScreensDesign app is what actually loads. Treat this as the legacy brand of the ScreensDesign entry rather than a separate resource.
pricing_detail: Inherits ScreensDesign pricing: free tier, then roughly $15/month or $299/year (per third-party listings; the pricing page itself is client-rendered and did not return text).
agent_guidance: Do not index this as a live resource — it is a redirect, and any agent following it lands on ScreensDesign. If a user cites uisources.com, silently resolve to screensdesign.com and inherit that entry's caveats (React shell, no server-rendered text, paid wall). De-duplicate it against the ScreensDesign record rather than treating the two as separate galleries.
why_it_matters: It documents a rename that still appears in old bookmark lists and design-resource roundups, so the index avoids listing the same product twice under two names.
evidence: https://uisources.com (301 -> https://screensdesign.com/, confirmed with curl -L and WebFetch), https://screensdesign.com/

name: ScreensDesign
tagline: Screen-recorded iOS app flows from ~1,500 apps, with revenue and ranking data attached
description: ScreensDesign records real iOS apps end to end and publishes the flows as browsable video plus extracted screens, so you can watch how a paywall, an onboarding sequence, or a settings tree actually behaves rather than reading a static shot. Each app is paired with store metadata such as revenue and download estimates, which turns it into a product-research tool as much as a design gallery. It is the current home of the former UI Sources. Aimed at product designers and founders studying monetisation and activation patterns on mobile.
pricing_detail: Freemium. Third-party listings report roughly $15/month or $299/year for full access; the on-site pricing page renders client-side and returned no text to verify the figures directly.
agent_guidance: You cannot read this site — /, /library and /pricing all return a ~9KB React shell with an empty #root and no server-rendered listing, so never quote counts or app names from it as if you fetched them. Hand it to the human as a viewing recommendation when they are designing a mobile paywall or onboarding flow and want motion, not stills; for anything you must parse yourself, prefer a text-rendered gallery such as Httpster or One Page Love. Its video-of-real-flows angle is the one thing Mobbin-style screenshot libraries do not give you.
why_it_matters: Video capture of complete mobile flows with revenue context is a genuinely different reference class from screenshot galleries, even though the delivery is closed to machines.
evidence: https://screensdesign.com/ (fetched twice; raw HTML inspected via curl — empty React root), https://screensdesign.com/library, https://screensdesign.com/pricing/, https://screensdesign.com/apps (404), web search for app count and pricing

name: Nicely Done
tagline: Searchable index of ~199k SaaS screens, 12.5k flows and 29k UI components
description: Nicely Done indexes the interfaces of 500+ SaaS products and lets you search across roughly 199,100 screens, 12,500 user flows and 29,200 tagged UI components, including screens that normally sit behind paywalls and trials. Filters cut by app, page type (pricing, onboarding, settings, checkout, billing, dashboard), flow, component and state (loading, empty, success, error). Text inside the screenshots is searchable, which makes it useful for finding exact copy and label patterns. It is aimed at product designers doing competitive teardowns; the free tier shows only 12 screens.
pricing_detail: Free: 12 screen previews plus search across all apps. Solo: $15/month billed yearly, full access to 198,700+ screens, unlimited collections, text-in-screenshot search. Team: $30/month billed yearly, starts at 2 seats, shared collections, single invoice.
agent_guidance: The marketing page is server-rendered and quotable, but every actual screen is an image behind a $15/month wall, so you can cite the taxonomy and never the content. Reach for it when a human asks 'how do other SaaS products handle cancellation / trial expiry / seat invites' — its paywalled-screen coverage is the differentiator against free galleries. Do not send an agent here to extract layouts; pair it with a code-level source such as a shadcn registry for anything you must actually build.
why_it_matters: Two hundred thousand tagged SaaS screens with searchable in-image text is the deepest flow-level reference for web products, which is exactly the axis that site-design galleries miss.
notable_for: screens from behind paywalls and trials

name: Curated.design
tagline: ~3,500 hand-picked product websites, now a section of the Craftwork marketplace
description: Curated.design is a gallery of well-made product and startup websites, each card carrying a one-line description, a static preview and a scroll-capture video. The domain now 301s to craftwork.design/curated/websites, where it lives as the inspiration wing of the Craftwork asset marketplace. Browsing is free and the entries are sorted into 15 industry categories with additional style and attribute filters. Newest entries at the time of check were dated 2026-08-11, so it is being fed regularly.
pricing_detail: The gallery is free to browse. The surrounding Craftwork marketplace sells assets and a 'Pro Access' subscription with a student discount; no price was shown on the pages fetched.
agent_guidance: This one you can actually parse: the Next.js RSC payload embeds each entry as JSON — id, name, slug, description, coverUrl, videoCover, externalReference, createdAt — right in the HTML of /curated/websites, so scrape that instead of trying to read the rendered grid. Use it to build a list of live sites in a given vertical (AI, fintech, developer tools) and then fetch those sites directly for real markup. Watch the redirect: requests to curated.design must follow the 301, and the surrounding page is a paid asset marketplace, so do not confuse marketplace product cards with gallery entries.
why_it_matters: Free, current, and machine-readable in a category where almost everything else is either login-walled or an opaque image grid.
notable_for: entry JSON embedded in the page payload
evidence: https://curated.design (301 -> https://craftwork.design/curated/websites), https://craftwork.design/curated/websites (324KB, RSC payload parsed for entry ids, names and createdAt), https://craftwork.design/curated

name: Httpster
tagline: 3,116 web designs, tagged by 19 visual styles and 29 industries, in plain HTML
description: Httpster has been collecting notable web design since 2012 and now lists 3,116 sites, each tagged by visual style and by business type with a live count next to every tag. Styles run Colourful (923), Brutalist (5), Dark (259), Fullscreen (273), Grid (647), Illustrative (282), Interactive (263), Light (673), Low carbon (3), Minimal (847), Monotone (52), Unusual Layout (663), Unusual Navigation (215), Photographic (1412), Print (3), Responsive (1106), Retro (62), Scrolling Behaviour (611) and Typographic (1193). Types cover 29 industries from Advertising to Travel, with Design & Illustration (1032), Showcase (610) and Ecommerce (456) the largest. No account, no paywall, no bot blocking.
agent_guidance: Best agent target in this batch: the homepage is static server-rendered HTML with every site name, its outbound link and a numeric count beside each tag, so a single fetch plus a tag-filtered URL gives you a real list of live URLs to go read for markup. Use it when a human asks for concrete examples of a named aesthetic — 'brutalist', 'unusual navigation', 'typographic' — because the tag counts tell you up front whether the bucket is 5 sites or 1,400. It only points at sites; it has no code, no screenshots you may reuse, and no licence to copy anything you find.
why_it_matters: A fourteen-year-old curation with counted style tags and no login is the cheapest way for a machine to turn a vague aesthetic brief into a list of real, fetchable sites.
notable_for: fully server-rendered, no login or bot wall
outbound links to every live site
evidence: https://httpster.net/ (fetched via WebFetch and curl; full tag list and per-tag counts read from raw HTML)

name: One Page Love
tagline: 9,079 one-page sites, 8,729 sections, 1,603 OG image references and 275 templates
description: One Page Love has curated single-page websites and landing pages since 2008 and now holds 9,079 One Pagers plus 8,729 individually clipped page sections, so you can browse a whole hero, pricing block or footer rather than a full site. Entries are filtered by genre (Portfolio, Landing Page, SaaS, Case Study, Launching Soon and ~30 more), style (Minimal, Brutalism, Glassmorphism, Editorial, Gradients, 3D and ~18 more), platform (Framer, Webflow, WordPress, Squarespace, Carrd, Figma Sites, Shopify and more), underlying tech (Tailwind CSS, GSAP, Next.js, shadcn/ui, Three.js and 30+ others) and 27 colours. A separate OG Image Gallery adds 1,603 link-preview references across more than 30 site types. A separate shop sells 275 one-page templates from free to $99. Browsing is free with no login.

templates.name: One Page Love Templates
templates.purpose: Shop of 275 single-page templates for Framer, Webflow, WordPress, Squarespace, Carrd, Shopify, Figma and hand-coded stacks (Bootstrap, Tailwind CSS, Next.js), priced free to $99.

templates.name: Page Sections library
templates.purpose: 8,729 individually clipped page sections — heroes, pricing blocks, footers, testimonials — for section-level rather than whole-page reference.

templates.name: OG Image Gallery
templates.purpose: 1,603 Open Graph images grouped by more than 30 site types. The types include landing pages, portfolios, products, apps, SaaS and ecommerce.

pricing_detail: Gallery is free. Templates are one-off purchases from free to $99, with common tiers at $29, $69, $79 and $99. Paid submission options exist for getting a site featured.
agent_guidance: Reach for this over Httpster when the brief is a single marketing page or a specific block — its section library lets you pull 'pricing block' or 'hero' examples in isolation, and its tech filter (Tailwind CSS, GSAP, Next.js, shadcn/ui) narrows to sites whose stack matches what you are actually building. Pages are server-rendered and readable, so you can extract outbound URLs and then fetch the real site for markup. Use `/og` when the task is a social link preview rather than a page layout. It exposes 1,603 references and type counts in server-rendered HTML. The templates are commercial products with their own licences — link them, never assume you may copy their code.
why_it_matters: Section-level clipping plus a tech-stack filter turns a taste gallery into something you can query the way a developer thinks, and an eighteen-year archive of landing pages has no real substitute.
notable_for: 1,603 OG image references by site type
filter by underlying tech including Tailwind and shadcn/ui
